pattern.crimePattern: a retired director strikes down the secretary of twenty-two years who is taking her envelope log to the prosecutor; his nephew burns the log and dumps the weapon, and the director forges her resignation
pattern.notes: Fictional house, firm, staff and family; the Riat Hills and Dunga beach are settings only. Raphael Oduya is the killer here but not Kivuli: the log shows him receiving every envelope, first from "4.12" on the fourth floor (Records), then "from Ukarimu, via M.". Benson repeats a lie he was told after the fact: an unknowing helper, not an accomplice.

ob.text: A cook reports a woman found dead at the foot of the terrace steps of a house in the Riat Hills above Kisumu: Mrs. Mbithe Kioko (58). The house belongs to Raphael Oduya, released on Thursday after his DCI interview.

facts.text: Mrs. Mbithe Kioko was found dead at the foot of the terrace steps at Raphael Oduya's house on Saturday morning.
Fall injuries, and one earlier blow to the side of her head.
Drag marks a metre long on the lowest steps, as if someone began to move her and stopped.
On the terrace table, a soapstone bird is missing from a set of three.
Rosa: at half past nine on Friday she heard Mama Mbithe on the terrace, high: "Monday, Raphael." Then a thud, and nothing.
Rosa: Okoth's car came up at ten past ten; her dog barked at someone on the steps and they went away. At eleven the incinerator was burning.
Rosa: Benson came out of the staff house at 22:15, when the car arrived, in his slippers.
One scrap in the ash, in Mbithe's hand: "…from 4.12 (Records) — to Registry (J.E.)…"
Mbithe's own copy of her pension form, signed last year.
Photocopies in Mbithe's bag: nine years of envelopes "from Ukarimu, via M." arriving at Oduya, and going on "to Registry (J.E.)", "to Kisumu (B.M.)", "to Mlinzi Bora".
Produced by Oduya's counsel: a typed resignation letter "from Mbithe Kioko", dated last week, citing ill health and stress.
The fellowship leader: Akinyi was at an overnight women's fellowship in Kisumu town, 19:00 to 06:00.
Jared's gate guard: Jared was home all night; nothing crossed the shared road but one car, at ten past ten.
Mutua's bus ticket and his employer: in Machakos all week.
Mutua: "Last month she told me, 'If anything happens to me, look in my handbag.'"
Records: Friday 21:41, Oduya called Okoth for 2 minutes.
Records: Okoth's car, Kisumu town 21:50, Riat Hills 22:10, Dunga beach 23:20, home 23:50.
Records: before 21:50 Okoth's phone and car were in Kisumu town; he reached the house at 22:10.
At Dunga beach: the missing soapstone bird, in shallow water.
Oduya's laptop: the resignation letter's file was created on Saturday at 07:15; a scan of Mbithe's pension-form signature sits on the desktop.
Okoth's car: ash on the boot mat; Mbithe's hair on the towel the bird was wrapped in.
Fingerprints taken from Oduya in detention.
Post-mortem: a blow to the side of the head from a heavy, smooth, rounded stone, before the fall.
Post-mortem: death on Friday between 21:30 and 22:00.
Comparison: the resignation's signature is a pixel-for-pixel copy of the pension-form signature, down to a tiny ink blot. Real signatures always vary.
Lab: Mbithe's blood in the bird's crevices and on the towel in Okoth's car.
Lab: Oduya's prints on the resignation letter.
Document lab: the signature was pasted digitally; the burned paper is the same ledger stock as the photocopied pages.

Oduya: "Mrs. Kioko resigned last week. She had been unwell."
Oduya: "I never received instructions from anyone. I was a director. I gave them."
Oduya, after a long silence: "I carried envelopes. Twelve years, from the fourth floor, then from the foundation. A postman with a pension. She typed it all." He won't say whose.

lawyered.line: My client is a retired public servant of thirty years. No comment.

interrogations.intro: Raphael Oduya sits very still beside Senior Counsel Abel Kimathi. Once reopened: "I was with my wife all evening. Mrs. Kioko resigned last week; she had been unwell."
Okoth keeps turning his car keys over. "I was in town all night. I didn't go to my uncle's."
Mrs. Akinyi Oduya sits upright. "My husband was with me all evening."
Benson stands by the staff-house door. "No car left the compound on Friday night."
Mutua, by phone from Machakos, is angry and crying. "We quarrelled about her house. I was in Machakos."
Jared leans on his stick at the gate. "Our road quarrel is ten years old. I was home."
Mama Rosa keeps her hand on her dog's head.

Senior Counsel Kimathi leans across and says something in his client's ear. Oduya says nothing.
Oduya looks at the two signatures side by side, and takes off his glasses.

"I carried envelopes. For twelve years I carried them, from the fourth floor, and then from the foundation. I was a postman with a pension. She typed it all." He will not say whose. Senior Counsel Kimathi ends the interview.

reconstruction.text: For twenty-two years Mbithe logs every sealed envelope: twelve years ago they come from "4.12", an extension on the fourth floor; for nine years "from Ukarimu, via M.". They go on to the registry, to a garage in Kisumu, to Mlinzi Bora.
After Pius's statement, on Friday afternoon, she tells Oduya she'll take the log to the prosecutor on Monday: "I typed your life for twenty-two years, Raphael."
At half past nine on the terrace he begs her; she refuses; he strikes her with a soapstone bird from the table and she falls down the steps. At 21:41 he calls Okoth.
Okoth burns the log's cover and forty pages, drives the bird to Dunga beach, and tries to move her until the dog barks. On Saturday at 07:15 Oduya types her "resignation".

afterVerdict.beat: Raphael Oduya is charged with Mbithe's murder and, on Pius's and Fundi's statements, as an accessory to the murder of Joseph Mwenda.

files.text: Raphael Oduya eliminated as Kivuli: the messenger. His secretary's log records him receiving every envelope from "4.12 (Records)", then "from Ukarimu, via M.".
Raphael Oduya charged as an accessory to the murder of Joseph Mwenda.

afterVerdict.beat: Mutua brings Amani the last thing in his mother's handbag, under the photocopies: "4.12 was Mrs. Kabiru's office. I took her envelopes up and down for three years. She always said 'Thank you, Mbithe.' She was always polite."
Mwalimu, on the phone: "Office 4.12. The corner office by the window. I told you I knew the corridor." Notebook: "One name left. 'Tell her it's done.' 'Thank you, Mbithe.'"

clockPlan.note: Three stamps (the maximum): records on the two lines and the tracker, a warrant on the study and one on Okoth's car. Oduya is reopened by the pasted signature. Detain him after the study warrant; prints (6 h), document (10 h) and blood (12 h) inside 24 h.
